correctness.rationale: The exact change \(s=x+y-1\), \(d=y-x\), \(\tau=\alpha t/2\) gives \(s^\prime=s(1-s^2-3d^2)\) and \(d^\prime=d(1-2\beta/\alpha-3s^2-d^2)\). Solving the factored equations for \(d>0\) exhausts the symmetric and asymmetric families. At the symmetric branch, physical eigenvalues are \(3\beta-\alpha\) and \(2\beta-\alpha\); hence it is a saddle whenever \(2\beta<\alpha<3\beta\). At the asymmetric branches, the scaled Jacobian determinant is \(2(1+k)(3k-1)<0\). At \(\alpha=3\beta\), the center-manifold equation is \(s^\prime=8s^3+O(s^5)\), showing nonlinear instability. At \(d=\varepsilon\) the noninteracting field points strictly outward at speed \(\beta\varepsilon\). Both eigenvalues strictly negative in the smooth confidence interior suffice for exponential local attraction. Symbolic verification confirms exact reductions, branch identities, critical cubic coefficient and rational examples; the algebraic proof, not finite experiments, establishes the all-parameter claims.
